text:
chris: Heads-up — we need a quick design discussion: partner/internally-issued API keys want different per-key limits and burst behavior than org defaults. Thinking: per-key policy objects + an opt-in console toggle for partners/internal services. Thoughts?
anya: +1 we have a few internal services that currently bypass org caps with hacks. Need a formal way. Security/approval workflow is key. :lock:
chris: Exactly. Two main asks from product/partners: 1) short high bursts (e.g., 1–2s spikes) for sync workflows, 2) sustained low QPS cap for billing predictability.
mike: Important to separate enforcement vs UI. Enforcement path: runtime should evaluate in this order: key override -> org policy -> default. No policy should allow unbounded requests. Also need audit trail for who granted the override.
sarah: From console UX: show per-key telemetry on the key detail page, with a simple "Override" button that opens an approval flow. Also surface last-30m usage, peak bursts, and a suggested safe burst value.
anya: Approval flow: product + infra leads sign-off, auto-expire after X days unless renewed. Also require justification string.
chris: For runtime knobs I'm proposing: qps_burst (burst tokens per window), qps_sustained (steady tokens/s), window_seconds, and a circuit_breaker_threshold (errors or latched failures). Example config:```yaml
key_policy:
  key: svc-internal-123
  qps_burst: 400
  qps_sustained: 50
  window_seconds: 60
  priority: high
  enforce: true
  expires_at: "2025-10-01T00:00:00Z"
  approved_by: "anya"
```
mike: That looks reasonable. A couple of infra notes: 1) Keep enforcement consistent across hosted/dedicated/private — in private deploys the policy should be synced but enforcement could be local. 2) We must avoid adding significant per-request latency for policy lookup. Cache policies keyed by key-id with TTL and watch for updates.
infra-bot: POLICY-CHANGE: detected new key_policy for svc-internal-123 by anya at 1823456795. Logging to audit stream: /audit/keys.
anya: Good. For telemetry I want a small metric set emitted per request: {key_id, route, latency_ms, decision: allowed|throttled|queued, token_cost}. Aggregations: per-minute p95 latency, burst_count, throttle_count.
sarah: Dashboards: new per-key panels (top 20 keys by QPS) + anomaly alert when throttle_rate > 1% for >5m. Also expose a CSV export for partner reports.
chris: Billing considerations — if partner keys have higher burst we should rate-limit billable tokens too. Suggest a flag: billable_override: true/false. If false, requests under override still count to org billing.
mike: Implementation detail — model routing: key-level priority can route to dedicated pools when available; fallback to hosted if capacity low. But that makes routing + billing coupled — need careful design.
anya: Security: keys that get elevated bursts should require MFA/2nd approver for >1k burst. Also restrict to keys flagged as "internal" or "trusted-partner".
chris: Agree. Edge cases: what happens when a key override is revoked mid-window? Propose: allow current window tokens to finish, then enforce new limits immediately for subsequent windows. Document behavior clearly.
sarah: UX wording: "Temporary burst grants" with expiry and renewal button. Keep default expiry to 7 days for internal dev, 90 days for long-term partners.
mike: We also need CLI support for ops: `rictl keys policy get <key>` and `rictl keys policy set --json policy.json`. Example quick check command:```bash
$ rictl usage show --key svc-internal-123 --window 60
key: svc-internal-123
window: 60s
requests: 12,345
throttled: 42
peak_burst: 380
current_policy: qps_burst=400 qps_sustained=50 enforce=true
```
anya: One more ask: expose a dry-run mode in console so partners can request a burst and see projected throttle risk for next 24h based on historical traffic. That'll reduce noisy approvals.
chris: Nice. Action items: 1) eng-platform: draft policy proto + runtime lookup/cache (mike) 2) console: key detail UI mock + approval flow (sarah) 3) security: approval rules + RBAC (anya) 4) infra-bot: hook to emit audit events (infra-bot / infra) — target RFC by EOW. Anyone object?
mike: No objections. I'll stub the proto and post a link to a repo PR.
anya: I'll write the approval matrix and add 2-approver rule for >1k burst.
sarah: I'll mock dumb UI and include CSV/export + dry-run UX.
chris: I'll own doc and sample policy YAML + update docs for rollout semantics. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
